rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Prescriptive optimization and constraint solving inside DuckDB, powered by Google OR-Tools. This is the decision-making complement to the predictive ML workers (predict / xgboost / lightgbm): instead of forecasting what will happen, it computes what you should *do* -- the lowest-cost assignment, the shortest set of routes, a feasible schedule, the maximum throughput of a network, or the most valuable way to pack a container.

Reach for this catalog when a question is a decision or feasibility problem rather than an aggregation: matching supply to demand at least cost, sequencing jobs on machines under precedence and resource limits, routing a fleet from a depot under capacity and time-window constraints, or any hand-built constraint model that mixes global constraints (all-different, no-overlap, cumulative, circuit) that LP/MIP solvers such as the community `highs` extension cannot express.

Key concepts. Problems are passed entirely as scalar arguments -- integer matrices and vectors built by `array_agg` (OR-Tools is an integer engine, so scale fractional data first), or, for the general constraint solver, a versioned JSON model. Build the cost, distance, or demand matrices using ordinary SQL joins, solve next to the data, and join the solution rows straight back into your warehouse -- no separate optimization microservice, data copy, or ETL round-trip. Every solver reports a `status`; a problem with no solution returns a single status row (test for the string INFEASIBLE, never an empty result), never an empty set.

The worker makes no outbound network calls -- pure local CPU, no API keys, no data egress. Your problem instances, which encode your customers and depots, never leave the box.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# Optimization & Constraint Solving in SQL (Google OR-Tools)

**Prescriptive compute inside DuckDB: constraint programming, vehicle routing, scheduling, assignment, network flow, and packing as plain SQL functions.**

This catalog turns [Google OR-Tools](https://developers.google.com/optimization) into DuckDB table and scalar functions, so an operations, logistics, or planning team that already lives in DuckDB can solve optimization problems next to their data instead of standing up a separate Python optimization microservice with its own deploy, data copy, and ETL round-trip.

## When to reach for it

Use it when a question is a *decision* problem rather than an aggregation -- matching supply to demand at least cost, sequencing work under precedence and resource limits, routing a fleet under capacity and time windows, maximizing the throughput of a network, or any hand-built constraint model mixing the global constraints (all-different, no-overlap, cumulative, circuit) that LP/MIP solvers such as the community `highs` extension stop short of. It is the decision-making complement to the predictive ML workers.

## How it works

Build the cost, distance, demand, or capacity matrices using ordinary SQL joins and `array_agg`, hand them to a solver as integer list arguments (OR-Tools is an integer engine -- scale fractional data first), and get the optimal or best-found solution back as rows you can join straight back into the warehouse. Every solver returns a `status` column, and a problem with no solution returns exactly one status row rather than an empty result.

## Data residency

The worker makes **no outbound network calls** -- pure local CPU, no API keys, no rate limits, no data egress. Your problem instances never leave the box. OR-Tools is Apache-2.0; the worker is MIT.
